title: US Job Market Growth Slows Significantly in September
subtitle: New data shows hiring has cooled as workers face rising prices and a difficult search for new roles.

summary.en: The United States job market added only 29,000 jobs in September, falling far below expert predictions. The unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2% as hiring slowed across several major industries. While widespread job losses are not occurring, finding new work has become more difficult for many Americans. Wages are currently rising by only 3%, which is likely not enough to keep up with the rising cost of living. These figures suggest that the Federal Reserve may be less likely to raise interest rates again before the upcoming midterm elections.
summary.zh: 美國九月就業市場僅增加兩萬九千個職位，遠低於專家預測。隨著多個主要產業招聘放緩，失業率微升至百分之四點二。雖然未出現大規模裁員，但許多美國人發現找工作變得更加困難。目前薪資僅成長百分之三，恐難以跟上生活成本的漲幅。這些數據顯示，聯準會在即將到來的期中選舉前，再次升息的可能性可能降低。

paragraphs.en: The United States job market showed clear signs of slowing down in September. According to the latest data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, employers added only 29,000 new jobs during the month. This number is much lower than what experts had predicted, as many had expected the economy to add nearly 70,000 jobs. This report comes as a significant drop from previous months and serves as a reminder that the labor market is cooling as the country approaches the midterm elections.
paragraphs.zh: 美國就業市場在九月出現了明顯的放緩跡象。根據美國勞工統計局（US Bureau of Labor Statistics）的最新數據，雇主在該月僅增加了兩萬九千個新職位。此數字遠低於專家的預測，因為許多人原本預期經濟將增加近七萬個職位。這份報告顯示就業成長較前幾個月大幅下滑，也提醒了人們隨著期中選舉臨近，勞動市場正在降溫。

paragraphs.en: This latest update follows a period of inconsistent growth. The government also revised earlier reports for July and August, lowering the total number of jobs added during those months by 60,000. In fact, after these revisions, the labor market actually lost 10,000 jobs in July. While August showed a stronger performance with 133,000 new jobs added, the overall trend suggests that the "slow-hire, slow-fire" environment continues to define the current economic landscape.
paragraphs.zh: 這項最新數據反映了一段成長不穩定的時期。政府同時修正了七月與八月的早期報告，將這兩個月的新增職位總數下修了六萬個。事實上，經過這些修正後，勞動市場在七月實際上減少了一萬個職位。儘管八月的表現較為強勁，增加了十三萬三千個新職位，但整體趨勢顯示，「慢聘、慢裁」的環境持續定義著當前的經濟景觀。

paragraphs.en: Most of the job growth in September was concentrated in the healthcare industry, which added 17,000 positions. However, other major sectors, including information, financial services, and professional industries, saw losses. NPR reports that while there are no signs of widespread job cuts, the lack of new hiring makes it difficult for people who are currently looking for work. Sarah House, a senior economist at Wells Fargo, noted that while workers are not seeing many layoffs, the lack of turnover makes it very hard for new workers or those returning to the workforce to get their foot in the door.
paragraphs.zh: 九月大部分的職位成長集中在醫療保健產業，該產業增加了一萬七千個職位。然而，包括資訊、金融服務與專業產業在內的其他主要領域則出現了職位流失。美國國家公共廣播電台（NPR）報導指出，雖然目前沒有大規模裁員的跡象，但缺乏新職缺使得求職者難以找到工作。富國銀行（Wells Fargo）資深經濟學家莎拉·豪斯（Sarah House）指出，雖然勞工並未面臨大量解僱，但職位流動率低，使得新進人員或重返職場者極難跨入就業門檻。

paragraphs.en: Another concern for many families is that wages are not keeping up with the rising cost of living. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics noted that average hourly earnings grew by only 3%, which is the lowest rate in over five years. Because prices for goods and services are rising faster than paychecks, the real buying power of the average American is decreasing. This is made worse by higher energy costs and rising interest rates. For example, mortgage rates recently jumped to their highest level in three years, reaching 7.28%. The Guardian Business reports that higher oil prices alone have cost the average American household an estimated $936.
paragraphs.zh: 另一個讓許多家庭擔憂的問題是薪資成長趕不上生活成本的攀升。美國勞工統計局指出，平均時薪僅成長百分之三，這是五年多來的最低水準。由於商品與服務價格的上漲速度快於薪資漲幅，一般美國人的實質購買力正在下降。能源成本增加與利率上升更讓情況雪上加霜。例如，房貸利率近期飆升至三年來最高水準，達到百分之七點二八。《衛報》商業版（The Guardian Business）報導，僅僅是油價上漲，就讓一般美國家庭估計多支出了九百三十六美元。

paragraphs.en: There are also differences in how different groups are experiencing these challenges. The unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2% in September, partly because more people entered the workforce to look for jobs. However, the data reveals that the impact is not equal. Unemployment among Black Americans rose to 7%, which is double the rate of white Americans. This gap highlights the uneven nature of the current economic recovery.
paragraphs.zh: 不同族群在面對這些挑戰時也有所差異。九月的失業率微升至百分之四點二，部分原因是更多人進入勞動力市場尋找工作。然而，數據顯示這種影響並非均等。非裔美國人的失業率上升至百分之七，是白人失業率的兩倍。這種差距凸顯了當前經濟復甦的不均衡本質。

paragraphs.en: These new figures have changed expectations for the Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States. The Fed recently raised interest rates—the cost of borrowing money—in an effort to control inflation, which is the general increase in prices over time. While the Fed chair, Kevin Warsh, previously emphasized that the labor market was strong, the cooling data makes it less likely that officials will raise rates again at their next meeting. Most experts now believe that any further rate increases will be delayed until the end of the year.
paragraphs.zh: 這些新數據改變了外界對美國中央銀行——聯準會（Federal Reserve）的預期。聯準會近期調升了利率（即借貸成本），旨在控制通貨膨脹，也就是物價隨時間普遍上漲的現象。雖然聯準會主席凱文·沃許（Kevin Warsh）先前強調勞動市場強勁，但降溫的數據使得官員在下次會議中再次升息的可能性降低。多數專家目前認為，任何進一步的升息行動都將延後至年底。

paragraphs.en: Despite the slower growth, some private sector data had previously suggested a more positive outlook. Earlier in the week, the payroll firm ADP reported that private hiring had actually increased, led by growth in hospitality and education. However, the official government data released on Friday paints a more cautious picture. As the country moves toward the November 3rd elections, the combination of slow job growth and high inflation remains the biggest economic challenge for the American public.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管成長放緩，一些民間部門的數據先前曾顯示出較為樂觀的前景。本週稍早，薪資處理公司 ADP 曾報導民間招聘實際上有所增加，主要由餐旅與教育產業帶動。然而，週五發布的官方政府數據則描繪出一幅較為謹慎的圖像。隨著國家邁向十一月三日的選舉，就業成長緩慢與高通貨膨脹的結合，依然是美國大眾面臨的最大經濟挑戰。

keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作形容詞（涼爽的），這裡指經濟活動減弱。文中：This report comes as a significant drop from previous months and serves as a reminder that the labor market is cooling as the country approaches the midterm elections.

keyTerms.term: get their foot in the door
keyTerms.definitionEn: To manage to enter a profession or organization at an entry level, often with the hope of future success.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 成功踏入某個領域或行業（通常指獲得入門機會）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是腳踏進門，這裡指獲得工作機會。文中：Sarah House, a senior economist at Wells Fargo, noted that while workers are not seeing many layoffs, the lack of turnover makes it very hard for new workers or those returning to the workforce to get their foot in the door.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To progress at the same speed as something else.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指薪資成長的速度趕不上物價上漲的速度。文中：Another concern for many families is that wages are not keeping up with the rising cost of living.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To describe or show something in a particular way.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（油漆）或動詞（繪畫），這裡指呈現出某種情境。文中：However, the official government data released on Friday paints a more cautious picture.

quiz.question: What happened to the job growth figures for July and August after the government's revision?

options.A: They were increased by a total of 60,000 jobs.
options.B: They were reduced by a total of 60,000 jobs.
options.C: They remained unchanged despite the slowing economy.
options.D: They showed that July had 133,000 new jobs added.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，政府修正了七月與八月的報告，將總新增職位數下修了 60,000 個。選項 A 剛好相反；選項 C 錯誤，因為數據確實有變動；選項 D 錯誤，因為 133,000 是八月修正後的數據，而非七月的數據，且該數字並未包含在下修的總額計算中。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might it be difficult for a recent college graduate to find a job in the current market?

options.A: Companies are conducting widespread layoffs of existing staff.
options.B: The healthcare sector is not hiring any new employees.
options.C: Low turnover rates mean fewer positions are becoming available.
options.D: The Federal Reserve has banned all new hiring to control inflation.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第三段提到，雖然沒有大規模裁員（layoffs），但「缺乏人員流動」（lack of turnover）使得新進人員或重返職場者難以進入職場。選項 A 與文意衝突；選項 B 錯誤，因為醫療業是少數有成長的產業；選項 D 為過度推論，聯準會是調整利率，並未禁止企業招募。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the phrase 'get their foot in the door' mean?

options.A: To gain an initial opportunity or entry into a field.
options.B: To physically block someone from entering a building.
options.C: To force a company to offer a higher starting salary.
options.D: To exit the workforce due to personal reasons.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。片語 'get one's foot in the door' 是慣用語，意指「獲得初步機會」或「進入某個領域的門檻」。文中提到因為缺乏職位流動，使得新人很難進入職場。選項 B 為字面誤解；選項 C 與 D 皆與職涯進入的語境無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the US economy?

options.A: The economy is rapidly recovering due to high hiring in the private sector.
options.B: Rising interest rates have successfully eliminated inflation in the US.
options.C: The job market is cooling, and economic challenges like inflation are putting pressure on households.
options.D: The upcoming midterm elections are the sole cause of the current economic downturn.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體論述了美國就業市場放緩、薪資成長追不上通膨、以及這些因素如何影響家庭生計，並導致聯準會對升息政策採取更審慎的態度。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 錯誤，因為通膨仍是挑戰；選項 D 雖然提到選舉，但僅作為背景，並非經濟低迷的唯一原因。
